newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures drift lower in very thin trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures drift lower in very thin trade.

text.p: IPE Brent futures drifted slightly lower on Friday in thin trade, with few traders expecting any major moves with NYMEX closed a second consecutive day for the Thanksgiving holiday.
Jan Brent was trading six cents lower at $22.54 a barrel, while Dec gas oil 50 cents lower at $217.00 a tonne.
"Volumes are very thin. There's really nothing going on," said one trader. "Jan's moving about a bit but it's just locals mucking about with the range".
"We saw the market come off on the Iraqi oil news yesterday but now its on hold," said another trader. "
News indicating the Iraqi-UN oil-for-food deal was nearing fruition pressured Brent futures lower in afternoon trade on Thursday.
Jan futures shed about 15 cents on Thursday afternoon after Turkish State Minister Lutfi Esengun said Iraqi oil would start flowing through a trans-Turkey pipeline by December.
But the market hardly batted an eyelid on the announcement of the price of Kirkuk Blend crude for December loading to for European customers by Iraq's state firm SOMO early on Friday.
"The market isn't going to do anything major until NYMEX comes back in," said a trader.
Dec gas oil was slightly lower but in extremely thin volume. Just 968 lots had traded by 1111 GMT.
Traders said weather conditions in Europe and the north-east United States would continue to be crucial for price direction.

Independent forecaster, Weather Services Corporation (WSC) said in its morning bullet that a cold November had resulted in a higher than normal heating demand, but added milder temperatures were seen for the start of December.
